newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Winbond limit up on huge wafer project.
newsitem.headline: Winbond limit up on huge wafer project.

text.p: Winbond Electronics Corp, one of Taiwan's leading chipmakers, surged at mid-morning on Thursday on word it was considering investing in a huge wafer project in the island's burgeoning southern Tainan science park.
After 75 minutes at 0215 GMT, Winbond was up the daily seven percent limit to T$58.5, while the overall index had gained 0.62 percent.
The Commercial Times newspaper said on Thursday Winbond would invest T$160 billion over 10 years to build one eight-inch and two 12-inch wafer plants in Tainan.
Winbond confirmed such a project was under consideration.
"We cannot confirm the figure now, but once we make the final decision, the investment amount will be around that level (of T$160 billion)," Winbond spokesman Mike Liu said.
Brokers said the plan further affirmed their forecasts of a sound outlook for the semiconductor industry.
"The repeated huge investment plans in the semiconductor industry further supports the expected sound outlook of the industry," said indepedent analyst Michael Hung.

Taiwan's top two chipmakers, Taiwan Semiconductor and United Microelectronics, have announced even bigger long-range wafer fab ventures since April, bolstering Taiwan's most important industrial sector.
"There is huge room for Taiwan's semiconductor makers to grow further," Hung said.

He said Taiwan's chipmakers account for some 3.5 percent of the global market share now. "Imagine oneday the local chip industry can expand to take a 10 percent pie of the global market. It has the best outlook among Taiwan's industries."
